transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you here?

Hi, thanks. Honestly, what made me finally come in is that I keep getting up during our long sales strategy meetings at work. I know I’m supposed to just stay seated, but I keep finding reasons to leave my chair... even if it’s just to refill my water or pace by the printer for a minute. It's just starting to become an issue.
Did you have similar trouble staying seated or sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. Actually, I remember this starting way before high school. Back in elementary school, my teachers would always write notes on my report cards saying that I was bright, but that I rushed through my work. They also mentioned that I talked out of turn a lot, forgot my homework, and... well, my desk was always just stuffed with half-finished papers. So, it's definitely been going on for a long time.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble staying still, even when you need to?

Yeah, mostly just in the way I mentioned about the meetings. I don't know if I'd call it a constant restlessness, but... sitting still for a long time just gets really uncomfortable. I just get this urge that I need to move or stretch my legs. But honestly, I haven't really noticed it too much outside of those long situations at work.
When you’re not able to sit still, do you also find yourself blurting things out or interrupting other people?

Yeah, I do. It happens a lot at work, actually. I'll often jump in with an answer before a client or one of my coworkers has even finished asking their question. And then... well, I usually realize I just answered the wrong thing because I didn't wait to hear the whole question, or I just realize I completely cut them off. It's definitely something I catch myself doing.
Have you often gotten into fights, threatened people, or deliberately broken rules or property?

No, not at all. I mean, I can be impatient and interrupt people, like I said, but I don't get into fights or threaten anyone. And I definitely don't go around breaking things or deliberately breaking rules. That's just not me.
Before age 12, did you also tend to be unusually fidgety or unable to stay seated when expected?

Yeah, I definitely did. I remember this all starting way before high school, honestly. My elementary school teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright but always rushed through things. They'd say I talked out of turn a lot, forgot my homework... and my desk was always just stuffed with half-finished papers. So, yeah, I've had a hard time sitting still and focusing for a long time.
Besides the interrupting and trouble sitting still, do you also often feel overly active or like you have to keep moving?

No, I wouldn't say I feel overly active like that. I mean, I get restless, sure, but I don't feel like I have a motor running inside me or anything where I just have to keep moving constantly. It's more just the fidgeting and having a hard time staying put in one spot for too long.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks once you’ve started them?

Yeah, I do. It happens a lot at work. Like, I'll get most of a sales proposal done, or I'll be updating the CRM system, and... I just leave off the very last step. I'll forget to actually send the final version of the proposal, or I won't log the follow-up in the system, even though I fully intended to finish the whole thing. It just kind of falls off my radar right at the end.
Do you also have these kinds of hyperactive or impulsive behaviors outside of work, such as at home or in other settings?

I haven't really noticed it being an issue at home, to be honest. I mean, work is definitely where the fidgeting and interrupting happens the most. But when I'm just at my house or out with friends... I don't think I really do those things. At least, it hasn't stood out to me as a problem in those situations.
Do you also have trouble sitting still or fidgeting at home or in other places outside of work?

No, not really. I mean, kind of like I just mentioned, it's really just at the office where I get like that. When I'm at home... I can sit on the couch and watch a movie or read just fine. I haven't noticed any fidgeting or trouble sitting still when I'm off the clock.
Do these attention problems, like losing track or not finishing tasks, also happen outside of work, such as at home or in social situations?

Not really, no. I mean... at home, I'm pretty good about getting things done. If I start cooking or doing laundry or something, I just finish it. And socially, I haven't really noticed any issues with losing track of things when I'm with my friends. It seems like the attention stuff is really just a problem for me when I'm on the clock.
Do you notice these problems in more than one setting, like both at work and at home or with friends?

No, like I mentioned a minute ago, it really is just at work. I don't notice any of these issues when I'm at home or hanging out with friends. So... yeah, it's really just the one setting where it's a problem for me.
Do you often feel like you can’t sit still when you’re at home or in other non-work settings?

No, not really. Like I mentioned a few minutes ago, I don't have any trouble sitting still when I'm at home. I can just relax on the couch without feeling like I need to be moving around or anything. It really is strictly an issue when I'm at the office.
Outside of interrupting people, do you often act without thinking first?

No, I wouldn't say so. I don't really have an issue with blurting things out or making impulsive decisions. I usually think things through before I do them. So, no, acting without thinking isn't really a problem for me.
Do you ever have these fidgeting or interrupting problems outside of work, like at home or in social situations?

No, um... like I said a couple of times now, it really is just at work. I don't fidget when I'm at home, and I don't interrupt my friends when we're hanging out. It's strictly an issue when I'm at the office.
Do you often feel like you’re driven by a motor or need to keep moving when you’re at work?

No, I don't really feel like that. I know I mentioned the fidgeting at my desk, but it's not like I have this intense urge to just keep moving constantly or anything. I don't feel like I'm driven by a motor. It's more just the small movements, not a need to be up and going all the time.
Do you often lose things like your keys, wallet, or phone in everyday life?

Yes, actually, I do. I'm constantly hunting for things I need for work. It's usually my headset, or client one-pagers... my keys, or even the notebook I was just using like ten minutes earlier. I just set things down and completely lose track of them.
When you were growing up, did teachers or parents often describe you as oppositional or defiant toward adults?
No, not really. Um, I was never described as oppositional or defiant or anything like that. I got along pretty well with my teachers and my parents growing up.
Do you often have difficulty paying close attention to details or make careless mistakes in your work?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I try to be pretty careful with my work. I might miss a tiny detail here or there, but it's not a regular thing where I'm making a bunch of careless mistakes on my accounts.
Before age 12, did you also often blurt out answers before questions were finished?

Yeah, I did. Um, I remember all of that starting way before high school, actually. My elementary school teachers used to write notes saying I was bright but rushed, and they definitely mentioned that I talked out of turn a lot. They also pointed out that I forgot my homework and just had a desk stuffed with half-finished papers.
